about: Each phrase's meaning, its support card ('phrase = meaning · word = meaning') and its explanation (phrase.<id>.meaning, .card, .explain).

strings.phrase.adios.explain: Say this when you leave. It means goodbye.
strings.phrase.adonde-vas.card: ¿Adónde vas? = Where are you going? · adónde = where to · vas = you go
strings.phrase.adonde-vas.explain: The fisher asks where you are going. Answer with voy a and the place.
strings.phrase.ayer-bebi-agua.card: Ayer bebí agua. = Yesterday I drank water. · bebí = I drank · agua = water
strings.phrase.ayer-bebi-agua.explain: Say you drank water yesterday. “Bebí” means “I drank”: -í, like comí.
strings.phrase.ayer-comi-fruta.card: Ayer comí fruta. = Yesterday I ate fruit. · comí = I ate · ayer = yesterday · fruta = fruit
strings.phrase.ayer-comi-fruta.explain: Say what you ate yesterday. “Comí” means “I ate”: the past form for “I” of comer. “Ayer” is yesterday.
strings.phrase.ayer-compre-fruta.card: Ayer compré fruta en la tienda. = Yesterday I bought fruit at the shop. · compré = I bought
strings.phrase.ayer-compre-fruta.explain: Luz tells you what she bought yesterday: compré, I bought. An -ar verb ends in -é for yo in the past.
strings.phrase.ayer-compre-fruta.meaning: Yesterday I bought fruit at the shop.
strings.phrase.ayer-fui-al-rio.card: Ayer fui al río. = Yesterday I went to the river. · fui = I went · río = river
strings.phrase.ayer-fui-al-rio.explain: Say you went to the river yesterday. “Fui” means “I went”: the past of ir, which does not follow the pattern.
strings.phrase.ayer-fui-al-rio.meaning: Yesterday I went to the river.
strings.phrase.ayer-trabajo-mucho.card: Ayer Domingo trabajó mucho. = Yesterday Domingo worked a lot. · trabajó = he worked
strings.phrase.ayer-trabajo-mucho.explain: Trabajó, he worked: an -ar verb ends in -ó for él and ella in the past. Mind the stress: trabajo is I work.
strings.phrase.ayuda.card: Ayuda. = Help. · necesito ayuda = I need help
strings.phrase.ayuda.explain: Say this to ask for help.
strings.phrase.bebiste-agua-ayer.card: ¿Bebiste agua ayer? = Did you drink water yesterday? · bebiste = you drank · agua = water
strings.phrase.bebiste-agua-ayer.explain: He asks if you drank water yesterday. “Bebiste” means “you drank”: -iste, like comiste.
strings.phrase.como-te-llamas.card: ¿Cómo te llamas? = What is your name? · te llamas = you are called (llamarse)
strings.phrase.como-te-llamas.explain: Ask someone's name: ¿Cómo te llamas? Te llamas is you are called; the answer is me llamo, I am called.
strings.phrase.compraste-dos-panes.card: Compraste dos panes. ¡Muy bien! = You bought two loaves. Very good! · compraste = you bought
strings.phrase.compraste-dos-panes.explain: Luz says what you bought: compraste, you bought.
strings.phrase.compraste-dos-panes.meaning: You bought two loaves. Very good!
strings.phrase.compre-dos-panes.card: Compré dos panes. = I bought two loaves. · compré = I bought
strings.phrase.compre-dos-panes.explain: Say what you bought: compré, the past of comprar for yo.
strings.phrase.cuanto-cuesta.card: ¿Cuánto cuesta? = How much is it? · cuánto = how much · cuesta = it costs
strings.phrase.cuanto-cuesta.explain: Ask the price: cuánto, how much, and cuesta, it costs (costar: cuesta for one, cuestan for more).
strings.phrase.cuantos-panes.card: ¿Cuántos panes quieres? = How many loaves do you want? · cuántos = how many
strings.phrase.cuantos-panes.explain: Luz asks how many loaves you want. Answer with a number: “Quiero dos panes, por favor”.
strings.phrase.cuantos-panes.meaning: How many loaves do you want?
strings.phrase.cuesta-dos-monedas.card: El pan cuesta dos monedas. = Bread costs two coins. · cuesta = costs · monedas = coins
strings.phrase.cuesta-dos-monedas.explain: A loaf costs two coins, so two loaves cost four.
strings.phrase.de-nada.card: De nada. = You are welcome. · de nada = you're welcome
strings.phrase.de-nada.explain: The polite answer to “gracias”. It means you are welcome.
strings.phrase.donde-esta-el-rio.card: ¿Dónde está el río? = Where is the river? · dónde = where · río = river
strings.phrase.donde-esta-el-rio.explain: Use this to ask where something is. “Dónde está” means where is.
strings.phrase.donde-esta-la-herreria.card: ¿Dónde está la herrería? = Where is the smithy? · herrería = smithy
strings.phrase.donde-esta-la-herreria.explain: Ask for another place the same way. Herrería ends in -a: la herrería.
strings.phrase.donde-esta-la-panaderia.card: ¿Dónde está la panadería? = Where is the bakery? · dónde está = where is · panadería = bakery
strings.phrase.donde-esta-la-panaderia.explain: Ask where a place is: “¿Dónde está…?” and the place with el or la. Panadería ends in -a: la panadería.
strings.phrase.donde-vives.card: ¿Dónde vives? = Where do you live? · vives = you live (vivir)
strings.phrase.donde-vives.explain: Domingo asks where you live. Answer with vivo, I live.
strings.phrase.el-letrero.card: El letrero dice: tienda, río, montaña. = The sign says: shop, river, mountain. · letrero = sign · dice = says
strings.phrase.el-letrero.explain: The villager reads the signpost where the road comes into the village.
strings.phrase.el-letrero.meaning: The sign says: shop, river, mountain.
strings.phrase.ella-quiere-fruta.card: Ella quiere fruta. = She wants fruit. · ella = she · quiere = wants · fruta = fruit
strings.phrase.ella-quiere-fruta.explain: Say what she wants. “Ella” means “she”, and “quiere” ends in -e for he or she.
strings.phrase.es-el-herrero.card: Es el herrero. = He is the smith. · es = he is · herrero = smith
strings.phrase.es-el-herrero.explain: Say who someone is: es and the job, with el (el herrero) or la.
strings.phrase.es-madera.card: ¿Es madera? = Is it wood? · es = it is · madera = wood
strings.phrase.es-madera.explain: Luna is asking whether something is wood. “Es” means “it is”.
strings.phrase.esta-a-la-izquierda.card: En el pueblo, mira la torre. La panadería está a la izquierda. = In the village, look at the tower. The bakery is on the left. · a la izquierda = on the left · torre = tower
strings.phrase.esta-a-la-izquierda.explain: The fisher says where the bakery is: looking at the tower, on the left. A la derecha is on the right.
strings.phrase.esta-a-la-izquierda.meaning: In the village, look at the tower. The bakery is on the left.
strings.phrase.esta-cerca.card: No, está cerca. La montaña está lejos. = No, it is near. The mountain is far. · cerca = near · lejos = far
strings.phrase.esta-cerca.explain: The fisher answers: the village is near, the mountain is far.
strings.phrase.esta-cerca.meaning: No, it is near. The mountain is far.
strings.phrase.esta-lejos.card: ¿Está lejos? = Is it far? · lejos = far · cerca = near
strings.phrase.esta-lejos.explain: Ask if a place is far. Where things are takes estar: está lejos, está cerca.
strings.phrase.fui-a-la-panaderia.card: Sí, fui a la panadería. = Yes, I went to the bakery. · fui = I went · panadería = bakery
strings.phrase.fui-a-la-panaderia.explain: Say you went: fui, the past of ir. The walk is over, so it is the past.
strings.phrase.fui-a-la-panaderia.meaning: Yes, I went to the bakery.
strings.phrase.fuiste-a-la-panaderia.card: ¿Fuiste a la panadería? = Did you go to the bakery? · fuiste = you went
strings.phrase.fuiste-a-la-panaderia.explain: The fisher asks about the walk you made. Fuiste is the past of ir for you.
strings.phrase.fuiste-a-la-panaderia.meaning: Did you go to the bakery?
strings.phrase.fuiste-al-rio-ayer.card: ¿Fuiste al río ayer? = Did you go to the river yesterday? · fuiste = you went · río = river
strings.phrase.fuiste-al-rio-ayer.explain: He asks if you went to the river yesterday. “Fuiste” means “you went”: the past of ir.
strings.phrase.fuiste-al-rio-ayer.meaning: Did you go to the river yesterday?
strings.phrase.gracias.explain: Say this when someone helps you. It means thank you.
strings.phrase.hay-pan.card: ¿Hay pan? = Is there any bread? · hay = is there
strings.phrase.hay-pan.explain: Ask if there is bread: hay, there is, and the noun.
strings.phrase.hay-tres-casas.card: En el pueblo hay una tienda, una panadería y tres casas. = In the village there is a shop, a bakery and three houses. · hay = there is, there are
strings.phrase.hay-tres-casas.explain: “Hay” is “there is” or “there are”, for one thing or many.
strings.phrase.hay-tres-casas.meaning: In the village there is a shop, a bakery and three houses.
strings.phrase.hay-un-pozo.card: ¿Hay un pozo en el pueblo? = Is there a well in the village? · hay = is there · pozo = well
strings.phrase.hay-un-pozo.explain: Ask if something is there with “¿Hay…?”. Pozo is masculine: un pozo.
strings.phrase.hay-un-pozo.meaning: Is there a well in the village?
strings.phrase.hizo-un-hacha.card: Domingo hizo un hacha. = Domingo made an axe. · hizo = he made
strings.phrase.hizo-un-hacha.explain: Say what someone made: hizo, the past of hacer for él and ella.
strings.phrase.hola.explain: Say this to greet anyone. It means hello.
strings.phrase.mas-despacio.card: Más despacio, por favor. = More slowly, please. · más = more · despacio = slowly
strings.phrase.mas-despacio.explain: Use this when the guide speaks too fast. She says her last line again, slowly.
strings.phrase.me-llamo-domingo.card: Me llamo Domingo. = My name is Domingo. · me llamo = I am called
strings.phrase.me-llamo-domingo.explain: The smith tells you his name: me llamo, I am called.
strings.phrase.me-llamo.card: Me llamo Luna. = My name is Luna. · me llamo = my name is
strings.phrase.me-llamo.explain: Luna is telling you her name. “Me llamo” means “my name is”.
strings.phrase.necesitamos-agua.card: Necesitamos agua. = We need water. · necesitamos = we need · agua = water
strings.phrase.necesitamos-agua.explain: Say what you and the villager need. “Necesitamos” means “we need”: the ending -amos is for “we”.
strings.phrase.necesitas-madera.card: Necesitas madera y frutas. = You need wood and fruit. · necesitas = you need · madera = wood · frutas = fruit
strings.phrase.necesitas-madera.explain: Luna is telling you what the camp needs. “Necesitas” means “you need”.
strings.phrase.necesito-agua.card: Necesito agua. = I need water. · necesito = I need · agua = water
strings.phrase.necesito-agua.explain: Say what you need. “Necesito” means “I need”: -o again, for “I”.
strings.phrase.necesito-madera-para-el-horno.car: Necesito cinco bloques de madera para el horno. Te pago cuatro monedas. ¿Qué vas a hacer? = I need five blocks of wood for the oven. I will pay you four coins. What are you going to do? · horno = oven · te pago = I will pay you
strings.phrase.necesito-madera-para-el-horno.exp: Luz needs wood for her oven and will pay four coins. Say your plan: “Voy a buscar madera”.
strings.phrase.necesito-madera-para-el-horno.mea: I need five blocks of wood for the oven. I will pay you four coins. What are you going to do?
strings.phrase.necesito-pan.card: Necesito pan. = I need bread. · necesito = I need · pan = bread
strings.phrase.no-gracias.explain: Say this to turn an offer down politely: no, thank you.
strings.phrase.no-se.explain: Say this when you do not know what to say. It is never wrong.
strings.phrase.no.explain: Say this to answer no to a question.
strings.phrase.otra-vez.card: Otra vez, por favor. = Again, please. · otra vez = again · por favor = please
strings.phrase.otra-vez.explain: Use this when you did not catch something. The guide says her last line again.
strings.phrase.pedir-agua.card: Quiero agua, por favor. = I want water, please. · quiero = I want · agua = water · por favor = please
strings.phrase.pedir-agua.explain: Use this to ask for something. “Quiero” means I want, and “por favor” means please.
strings.phrase.que-buscas.card: ¿Qué buscas? = What are you looking for? · buscas = you are looking for
strings.phrase.que-buscas.explain: The fisher asks what you are looking for. Answer with the place: “¿Dónde está la panadería?”.
strings.phrase.que-comiste-ayer.card: ¿Qué comiste ayer? = What did you eat yesterday? · comiste = you ate · ayer = yesterday
strings.phrase.que-comiste-ayer.explain: The shopkeeper asks what you ate yesterday. “Comiste” means “you ate”: a past form for “you”.
strings.phrase.que-compraste.card: ¿Qué compraste? = What did you buy? · compraste = you bought
strings.phrase.que-compraste.explain: Luz asks what you bought. Answer in the past: “Compré dos panes”.
strings.phrase.que-es-esto.card: ¿Qué es esto? = What is this? · qué = what · esto = this
strings.phrase.que-es-esto.explain: Use this to ask what something is. “Qué” means what and “esto” means this.
strings.phrase.que-haces.card: ¿Qué haces? = What do you do? · haces = you do (hacer)
strings.phrase.que-haces.explain: Ask someone what they do: ¿Qué haces? Hacer is to do or to make.
strings.phrase.que-hizo-domingo.card: ¿Qué hizo Domingo? = What did Domingo make? · hizo = he made
strings.phrase.que-hizo-domingo.explain: The villager asks what Domingo made. Answer in the past: hizo.
strings.phrase.que-necesita-usted.card: ¿Qué necesita usted? = What do you need? · usted = you (polite) · necesita = needs
strings.phrase.que-necesita-usted.explain: The shopkeeper asks what you need, politely. “Usted” is the polite “you”, and its verb ends like he or she: “necesita”.
strings.phrase.que-necesitas.card: ¿Qué necesitas? = What do you need? · necesitas = you need
strings.phrase.que-necesitas.explain: The shopkeeper is asking what you need.
strings.phrase.que-quiere-luna.card: ¿Qué quiere Luna? = What does Luna want? · quiere = he or she wants
strings.phrase.que-quiere-luna.explain: The villager asks what Luna wants. “Quiere” means “he or she wants”: the ending -e.
strings.phrase.que-quieren-ustedes.card: ¿Qué quieren ustedes? = What do you all want? · ustedes = you all · quieren = you all want
strings.phrase.que-quieren-ustedes.explain: The shopkeeper asks you both. “Ustedes” means “you all”, and “quieren” ends in -en.
strings.phrase.que-quieres.card: ¿Qué quieres? = What do you want? · quieres = you want · qué = what
strings.phrase.que-quieres.explain: Luna is asking what you want. “Quieres” means “you want”: the ending -es is for “you” (tú).
strings.phrase.que-va-a-hacer-domingo.card: ¿Qué va a hacer Domingo? = What is Domingo going to make? · va a hacer = he is going to make
strings.phrase.que-va-a-hacer-domingo.explain: The villager asks what Domingo is going to make. Answer for him: va a hacer.
strings.phrase.que-va-a-hacer-domingo.meaning: What is Domingo going to make?
strings.phrase.que-vamos-a-comer.card: ¿Qué vamos a comer? = What are we going to eat? · vamos a comer = we are going to eat
strings.phrase.que-vamos-a-comer.explain: The villager asks what the two of you will eat. “Vamos a comer” means “we are going to eat”.
strings.phrase.que-vamos-a-comer.meaning: What are we going to eat?
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-comer.card: ¿Qué vas a comer mañana? = What are you going to eat tomorrow? · vas a comer = you are going to eat · mañana = tomorrow
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-comer.explain: The villager asks what you will eat tomorrow. “Vas a comer” means “you are going to eat”: ir, a and an infinitive.
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-comer.meaning: What are you going to eat tomorrow?
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-hacer-alli.card: ¿Qué vas a hacer allí? = What are you going to do there? · vas a hacer = you are going to do · allí = there
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-hacer-alli.explain: The fisher asks your plan. Answer with voy a and a verb in the infinitive.
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-hacer-alli.meaning: What are you going to do there?
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-hacer.card: ¿Qué vas a hacer mañana? = What are you going to do tomorrow? · vas a hacer = you are going to do · mañana = tomorrow
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-hacer.explain: He asks what you are going to do tomorrow. “Vas a hacer” means “you are going to do”.
strings.phrase.que-vas-a-hacer.meaning: What are you going to do tomorrow?
strings.phrase.queremos-pan.card: Queremos pan. = We want bread. · queremos = we want · pan = bread
strings.phrase.queremos-pan.explain: Say what you both want. “Queremos” means “we want”.
strings.phrase.quieres-fruta.card: ¿Quieres fruta? = Would you like some fruit? · quieres = you want · fruta = fruit
strings.phrase.quieres-fruta.explain: Luna is offering you some fruit. “Quieres” means “do you want”.
strings.phrase.quieres-pan.card: ¿Quieres pan? = Would you like bread? · pan = bread · quieres = you want
strings.phrase.quieres-pan.explain: The shopkeeper is offering you bread.
strings.phrase.quieres-un-hacha.card: ¿Quieres un hacha? Necesito dos bloques de madera y dos monedas. = Do you want an axe? I need two blocks of wood and two coins. · hacha = axe · necesito = I need
strings.phrase.quieres-un-hacha.explain: Domingo will make you an axe for two wood and two coins.
strings.phrase.quieres-un-hacha.meaning: Do you want an axe? I need two blocks of wood and two coins.
strings.phrase.quiero-dos-panes.card: Quiero dos panes, por favor. = I want two loaves, please. · dos panes = two loaves
strings.phrase.quiero-dos-panes.explain: Ask for a number of loaves: quiero, the number and the plural, panes. At the bakery it is a purchase: a loaf costs two coins.
strings.phrase.quiero-madera.card: Quiero madera. = I want wood. · quiero = I want · madera = wood
strings.phrase.quiero-madera.explain: Say what you want. “Quiero” means “I want”: the ending -o is for “I” (yo).
strings.phrase.seis-a-diez.card: Seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez. = Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
strings.phrase.seis-a-diez.explain: Luz counts on: six to ten.
strings.phrase.si-por-favor.explain: Say this to accept an offer politely: yes, please.
strings.phrase.si.explain: Say this to answer yes to a question.
strings.phrase.soy-el-herrero.card: Soy el herrero. Trabajo con fuego y madera. = I am the smith. I work with fire and wood. · herrero = smith · trabajo = I work
strings.phrase.soy-el-herrero.explain: Domingo is the smith. Trabajo is I work; for him it is trabaja.
strings.phrase.soy-el-herrero.meaning: I am the smith. I work with fire and wood.
strings.phrase.tengo-botella.card: Tengo una botella. = I have a bottle. · tengo = I have · botella = bottle
strings.phrase.tengo-botella.explain: Say that you have a bottle. “Tengo” means “I have”.
strings.phrase.tengo-cuatro-monedas.card: Tengo cuatro monedas. = I have four coins. · tengo = I have · monedas = coins
strings.phrase.tengo-cuatro-monedas.explain: Say how many coins you have: tengo, the number and the plural, monedas.
strings.phrase.tengo-diez-panes.card: Tengo diez panes. = I have ten loaves. · panes = loaves (un pan, dos panes) · diez = ten
strings.phrase.tengo-diez-panes.explain: Luz has ten loaves. Pan, panes: a word that ends in a consonant takes -es for more than one.
strings.phrase.tengo-fruta.card: Tengo una fruta. = I have a fruit. · tengo = I have · fruta = fruit
strings.phrase.tengo-fruta.explain: Say that you have one. “Tengo” means “I have”. Tener also changes in the middle: tengo (I have), tienes (you have).
strings.phrase.tienes-fruta.card: ¿Tienes una fruta? = Do you have a fruit? · tienes = you have · fruta = fruit
strings.phrase.tienes-fruta.explain: Luna asks if you have a fruit. “Tienes” means “you have”.
strings.phrase.toma-cuatro-monedas.card: ¡Gracias! Toma cuatro monedas. = Thank you! Here are four coins. · toma = here you are · cuatro = four
strings.phrase.toma-cuatro-monedas.explain: Luz thanks you for the wood and pays you four coins.
strings.phrase.toma-cuatro-monedas.meaning: Thank you! Here are four coins.
strings.phrase.toma-el-hacha.card: ¡Gracias! Toma el hacha. = Thank you! Here is the axe. · toma = here you are · el hacha = the axe
strings.phrase.toma-el-hacha.explain: Domingo thanks you and gives you the axe.
strings.phrase.toma-el-hacha.meaning: Thank you! Here is the axe.
strings.phrase.trabaja-en-la-herreria.card: Domingo trabaja en la herrería. = Domingo works at the smithy. · trabaja = he works · herrería = smithy
strings.phrase.trabaja-en-la-herreria.explain: Say where someone works: trabaja en and the place. Trabajo is I work; trabaja, he or she works.
strings.phrase.uno-a-cinco.card: Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco. = One, two, three, four, five.
strings.phrase.uno-a-cinco.explain: Luz counts her loaves: one to five.
strings.phrase.va-a-hacer-un-hacha.card: Va a hacer un hacha. = He is going to make an axe. · va a hacer = he is going to make · hacha = axe (un hacha, el hacha)
strings.phrase.va-a-hacer-un-hacha.explain: Say what someone is going to do: va a and the infinitive. Hacha is feminine but takes un and el.
strings.phrase.va-a-hacer-un-hacha.meaning: He is going to make an axe.
strings.phrase.vamos-a-comer-fruta.card: Vamos a comer fruta. = We are going to eat fruit. · vamos a comer = we are going to eat · fruta = fruit
strings.phrase.vamos-a-comer-fruta.explain: Say what you will eat together. “Vamos a comer” means “we are going to eat”; said as a suggestion it also means “let's eat”.
strings.phrase.vamos-a-comer-fruta.meaning: We are going to eat fruit.
strings.phrase.vive-en-la-casa.card: Domingo vive en una casa cerca de la herrería. = Domingo lives in a house near the smithy. · vive = he lives · cerca de = near
strings.phrase.vive-en-la-casa.explain: Vive is he or she lives; vivo, I live.
strings.phrase.vive-en-la-casa.meaning: Domingo lives in a house near the smithy.
strings.phrase.vivo-en-el-campamento.card: Vivo en el campamento. = I live at the camp. · vivo = I live · campamento = camp
strings.phrase.vivo-en-el-campamento.explain: Say where you live: vivo en and the place.
strings.phrase.voy-a-buscar-madera.card: Voy a buscar madera. = I am going to look for wood. · voy a buscar = I am going to look for
strings.phrase.voy-a-buscar-madera.explain: Say your plan: voy a and an infinitive. Buscar is to look for.
strings.phrase.voy-a-buscar-madera.meaning: I am going to look for wood.
strings.phrase.voy-a-comer-pan.card: Voy a comer pan. = I am going to eat bread. · voy a comer = I am going to eat · pan = bread
strings.phrase.voy-a-comer-pan.explain: Say what you are going to eat. “Voy a comer” means “I am going to eat”: voy (from ir), a, and the infinitive comer.
strings.phrase.voy-a-comer-pan.meaning: I am going to eat bread.
strings.phrase.voy-a-comprar-pan.card: Voy a comprar pan. = I am going to buy bread. · voy a comprar = I am going to buy · pan = bread
strings.phrase.voy-a-comprar-pan.explain: Say your plan: voy a and an infinitive. Comprar is to buy.
strings.phrase.voy-a-comprar-pan.meaning: I am going to buy bread.
strings.phrase.voy-a-ir-al-rio.card: Mañana voy a ir al río. = Tomorrow I am going to go to the river. · voy a ir = I am going to go · mañana = tomorrow · río = river
strings.phrase.voy-a-ir-al-rio.explain: Say you will go to the river tomorrow: “voy a ir” is “I am going to go”. Yesterday it was “fui”.
strings.phrase.voy-a-ir-al-rio.meaning: Tomorrow I am going to go to the river.
strings.phrase.voy-a-la-panaderia.card: Voy a la panadería. = I am going to the bakery. · voy a = I am going to · panadería = bakery
strings.phrase.voy-a-la-panaderia.explain: Say where you are going now: voy, a, and the place.
strings.phrase.voy-a-la-panaderia.meaning: I am going to the bakery.
